items.content_html:
Description

Update the HTML Sanitizer API overview and all six Element, ShadowRoot, and Document method references to describe sanitization during parsing rather than a separate pass over the completed DOM. Explain the observable consequences for adjacent text nodes, custom element construction, resource-fetching side effects, and declarative shadow roots, with a focused example showing a replaced <b> producing one text node.

Also correct the default-sanitizer example to pass { sanitizer: "default" } to setHTMLUnsafe(), fix its inconsistent variable names and whitespace output, and clarify fragment parsing's top-level shadow-template behavior.

Motivation

The HTML Standard changed in whatwg/html#12756. The existing descriptions still teach the earlier parse-then-sanitize model and the unsafe example currently omits the sanitizer it claims to use. This documents the current specification and notes that some browsers still sanitize after parsing, producing different DOM structures.

Additional details

  • Specification: whatwg/html#12756 (merged).
  • Associated web-platform tests: web-platform-tests/wpt#62492, including custom element construction and declarative shadow-root cases.
  • Addresses the review at #46132 (comment).
  • Validation: Markdown lint, front-matter lint, Prettier, CSpell, and git diff --check passed for the changed content.
  • Built all seven changed pages with Rari: no issues reported. After the separate source/diff review and wording refinements, rebuilt all seven pages and checked formatting again: no issues reported.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #46132.

Related to #46148 (the release-note task); this PR updates the overview and API references.
items.title: Document sanitization during HTML parsing

items.content_html:
Fixes #42516.

The main questions I have are:

1. What exactly the conditions are for conditional mediation. The spec is quite opaque here:

For create(), if a user has previously consented to credential creation and the user agent knows it recently mediated an authentication, then the create() call may resolve without additional prominent modal interaction. If the user agent did not recently mediate an authentication or does not have consent for credential creation, then the call must throw a "NotAllowedError" DOMException.

(https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-credential-management/#mediation-requirements).

I've glossed this based on Ricky Mondello's talk (http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=otObbUSxcqs&t=10m50s) and the web.dev guide (https://developer.chrome.com/docs/identity/webauthn-conditional-create#how_it_works)

2. What the mediation option to create() means for other credential types, such as passwords. AFAICS the spec says nothing here. Testing suggests that it is just ignored.

3. What mediation values other than conditional mean for public key credentials. Again AFAICS they are just ignored, so I've opted not to list them even though they are in the IDL.

Also, I think we should take all this stuff out and into a separate guide page, but in a follow-up, please.
items.title: Document conditional create

items.content_html:
Description

This PR contains a 1 line copy change that hopefully clarifies an ambiguity in the <dashed-ident> docs around their user-defined nature.

Motivation

I was a little confused when I read the second clause here:

However, some `<custom-ident>`s are defined by the CSS language itself; `<dashed-ident>`s will never be defined in CSS.

The second clause is echoing the previous clause that mentions the CSS language, but I didn't interpret it that way at first. in CSS feels a bit too generic to me: is it referring to the CSS language, or CSS in general, the latter of which would include user-authored CSS.

I feel like contrasting against the first clause by stating that dashed idents will always be defined by the user helps highlight the difference and avoids this confusion.

That being said, maybe it was worded this way for a nuanced reason that I'm not aware of, so please provide feedback if that's the case.
items.title: Clarify user-defined nature of `<dashed-ident>`s

Title: [Technical review] Add BiDi network pages: addIntercept, continueRequest, failRequest, removeIntercept

Description

  • Added pages for the following commands of the network module:
    • network.addIntercept
    • network.continueRequest
    • network.failRequest
    • network.removeIntercept
  • Added an "Intercepts" section to the network module landing page.

The pages link to the event pages from #46141 and to network.setExtraHeaders from #46140, so this PR should merge after those two.

Every example was run against Firefox Nightly 159 and Chrome 155 (through ChromeDriver) with a local server.

Spec links

  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#command-network-addIntercept
  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#command-network-continueRequest
  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#command-network-failRequest
  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#command-network-removeIntercept

Related issue

Doc issue: mdn/mdn#851

Compat quirks worth looking into:

  • Compat data for the continueRequest parameters in Firefox. All three come from my test run:
    • url: for a fetch(), the rewritten request reaches the new URL and the events report a 200 from it, but the page's fetch() rejects with AbortError: The operation was aborted. A navigation with a rewritten URL works. BCD shows Firefox's url parameter as supported since 133. cc @whimboo for the compat sheet update.
    • headers: Firefox sends only the headers in the list, so a list without Host produces a request with no Host header (my server answered 400). Chrome still sends Host, Cookie, User-Agent and its other network headers. BCD shows Firefox's headers parameter as supported. cc @whimboo for the compat sheet update.
    • body: with a longer body for a POST request, Firefox keeps the original Content-Length, so the server receives a truncated body. Chrome sends the new length. BCD shows Firefox's body parameter as supported. cc @whimboo for the compat sheet update.
items.title: [Technical review] Add BiDi network intercept command pages

Updates cspell from 10.3.6 to 10.4.0

Release notes

Sourced from cspell's releases.

v10.4.0

Features

feat: Add --glob-symlinks to follow symbolic links when matching globs (#9342)

Summary

cspell lint can now follow symbolic links in glob searches, with --glob-symlinks. Glob searches skip linked files and linked directories by default, so a tree made of links, such as Bazel runfiles, found nothing to check.

Closes #7700.

Feature

cspell lint --glob-symlinks "**"
  • --glob-symlinks follows symbolic links, and searches linked directories, when matching globs. Links are followed wherever they point.
  • CSPELL_GLOB_SYMLINKS=true does the same for a whole job. --no-glob-symlinks overrides it.
  • API: globSymlinks in the lint options.
  • It can't be set in a configuration file.
  • Files are reported by the path through the link. A file reached by two paths is checked under both.
  • It applies only to glob searches. For --file, --files, and --file-list documents, use --follow-symlinks.
  • The design decisions are recorded in docs/ADRs/glob-symlinks/.
  • Link loops, such as a link to a parent directory, are stopped by the glob search after one level.

feat: Respect COLUMNS for help and table width (#9358)

Summary

Help, and the tables from cspell trace and cspell dictionaries, now follow the COLUMNS environment variable. That lets you choose a narrower width, which helps with large fonts and screen magnifiers. The help in the cspell README now fits on npmjs.com without scrolling sideways.

Description

Adds MDN reference pages for the WebAssembly reference instructions: a landing page plus one page per instruction in the spec's "Reference Instructions" section, along with a sidebar entry and a bullet on the WebAssembly reference index.

New pages:

  • WebAssembly/Reference/Reference: landing page
  • WebAssembly/Reference/Reference/null: ref.null
  • WebAssembly/Reference/Reference/is_null: ref.is_null
  • WebAssembly/Reference/Reference/func: ref.func
  • WebAssembly/Reference/Reference/as_non_null: ref.as_non_null
  • WebAssembly/Reference/Reference/eq: ref.eq
  • WebAssembly/Reference/Reference/test: ref.test
  • WebAssembly/Reference/Reference/cast: ref.cast

Also updated:

  • files/sidebars/webassemblysidebar.yaml: new "Reference" listSubPages entry under Instructions
  • files/en-us/webassembly/reference/index.md: new "WebAssembly reference instructions" bullet

Motivation

These instructions were missing from MDN's Wasm reference (#37854). As agreed with @chrisdavidmills, the instruction pages follow the structure of the add128 page, and the section follows the Table instructions landing page.

Additional details

How the examples were tested:

  • Each page's interactive example (the WAT and the JS loader exactly as written) was compiled with @mdn/watify, the compiler MDN uses for {%wasm-url%}. It was then run in Node 24 (V8), and the logged output matches the comments in each example.
  • The trapping and edge-case behavior described in the prose was tested with separate modules:
    • ref.as_non_null and ref.cast trap with a RuntimeError (on null, and on a type mismatch).
    • A nullable cast target lets null through.
    • ref.func fails validation without a declaration, and an export or global initializer counts as one.
    • ref.eq treats null as equal to null, compares i31refs by value, and rejects externref operands.
  • The binary encodings come from the WAT compiler's output and match spec §5.4.6. ref.test and ref.cast list both the nullable and non-nullable encodings.
  • lint:md, lint:fm, lint:typos and lint:yml pass. All pages render locally with npm start, with no broken links.

Expected flaw until the BCD data is released: each instruction page reports Unknown browser-compat entry: webassembly.instructions.ref_* for {{Compat}}, and {{Specifications}} is empty, because the keys are added in the BCD PR below.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #37854

Fix #42236. Continues #42267.

We have two documents that have basically identical structure and identical verbiage (presumably the observatory docs copied us, or we both copied from the spec explainer). I'm consolidating them both into security. I have no preference whether to put it in HTTP or security, but since we already have a central place for all security-related features we might as well use it as much as possible.

The major confusion was around which headers are sent by the embedder and which are sent by the resource, and how COEP/COOP/CORP work together. This rewrite hopefully adds that context.

Co-Authored-By: ajayojha oojhaajay@gmail.com
